pr_title: Lazily deserialize job arguments in test helper
pr_body:
### Summary

If there is a job in `enqueued_jobs` whose arguments are not deserializable for some reason (for example, a deleted ActiveRecord model) `assert_enqueued_with` will raise an error even if the job we're looking for is in the `enqueued_jobs` array.

This solution isn't as tidy as I was hoping for - definitely open to suggestions on other approaches!

### Other Information

Fixes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/39606

issue_context.title: `assert_enqueued_with` somewhat unexpectedly raises `ActiveJob::DeserializationError`
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

[Failing test](https://gist.github.com/BrentWheeldon/12844b2aeb4c0b5ed4a6b4a8b96657ac)

I've tried to explain this in words a couple of times and can't find a succinct way of explaining it. Essentially `assert_enqueued_with` will fail with a `ActiveJob::DeserializationError` if there is a job whose arguments won't deserialize (for example, the arguments contain a deleted ActiveRecord model) in the `enqueued_jobs` array before the job that we're trying to assert was enqueued.

### Expected behavior

The assertion passes - we don't blow up if some earlier job in the `enqueued_jobs` array has arguments that can't be be deserialized

### Actual behavior

`ActiveJob::DeserializationError` is raised from [`ActiveJob::TestHelper#deserialize_args_for_assertion `](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/49baf092439fc74fc3377b12e3334c3dd9d0752f/activejob/lib/active_job/test_helper.rb#L694)

### System configuration
**Rails version**:

`master@49baf09`

**Ruby version**:

`ruby 2.7.1p83 (2020-03-31 revision a0c7c23c9c) [x86_64-darwin19]`

review_comments:
It seems like this doesn't solve the problem in the general case, since an `ActiveJob::DeserializationError` can still blow up the assertion if `:job` isn't specified, no?

Also, I think `assert_performed_with` needs similar protection.  Something like the following would cause the same problem:

```ruby
model = Model.create!
ModelJob.perform_later(model)
perform_enqueued_jobs
model.destroy
assert_performed_with(job: ModelJob)
```

Perhaps we could rescue `ActiveJob::DeserializationError` in [`deserialize_args_for_assertion`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/1a7be948426a7300a8ea5a2cdb4c55d645b2552c/activejob/lib/active_job/test_helper.rb#L694)?  Although I'm not clear on whether we should attempt to [match](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/1a7be948426a7300a8ea5a2cdb4c55d645b2552c/activejob/lib/active_job/test_helper.rb#L408-L414) such jobs afterwards or not... :thinking:

Yeah - this definitely isn't a "fix all scenarios" patch, just make it less likely to fail 😓 

The new scenario you raise is a super interesting one (and solving that might make this a more robust solution). I'll pick this back up later in the week and see what I can come up with.

Thanks for taking a look and giving some feedback, @jonathanhefner!
